queries.label: prefix-tail-medium
queries.prompt: Explain why compiled model artifacts reduce cold-start latency. Focus on TTFT and GPU serving. Cover weight loading, tokenizer startup, CUDA context creation, graph warmup, memory mapping, and give one practical autoscaling deployment example.

queries.label: prefix-tail-long
queries.prompt: Explain why compiled model artifacts reduce cold-start latency. Focus on TTFT and GPU serving. Cover weight loading, tokenizer startup, CUDA context creation, graph warmup, memory mapping, and give one practical autoscaling deployment example. Compare precompiled artifacts with loading a raw checkpoint at request time. Mention pod churn, startup jitter, scheduler readiness, and why repeated deserialization hurts cold-start behavior.

queries.label: prefix-tail-xlong
queries.prompt: Explain why compiled model artifacts reduce cold-start latency. Focus on TTFT and GPU serving. Cover weight loading, tokenizer startup, CUDA context creation, graph warmup, memory mapping, and give one practical autoscaling deployment example. Compare precompiled artifacts with loading a raw checkpoint at request time. Mention pod churn, startup jitter, scheduler readiness, and why repeated deserialization hurts cold-start behavior. Explain how artifact reuse avoids repeated tensor remapping, shape validation, quantization metadata loading, kernel selection, KV cache planning, and other runtime setup work. End with three operational tips for keeping latency stable during scale-out events.

queries.label: prefix-tail-xxlong
queries.prompt: Explain why compiled model artifacts reduce cold-start latency. Focus on TTFT and GPU serving. Cover weight loading, tokenizer startup, CUDA context creation, graph warmup, memory mapping, and give one practical autoscaling deployment example. Compare precompiled artifacts with loading a raw checkpoint at request time. Mention pod churn, startup jitter, scheduler readiness, and why repeated deserialization hurts cold-start behavior. Explain how artifact reuse avoids repeated tensor remapping, shape validation, quantization metadata loading, kernel selection, KV cache planning, and other runtime setup work. Also discuss container cold boot, filesystem reads, safetensors parsing, host to device transfers, health-check deadlines, warm pool design, and graph capture readiness. Include a concrete example involving a bursty inference API, multiple fresh GPU replicas, a strict TTFT SLO, and the difference between prebuilt artifacts and ad hoc initialization. Finish with a short checklist for observability, rollback, and cache invalidation.
